summary: totp-utils postinstall harvests browser/Discord/Minecraft credentials and drops a remote JAR into Minecraft mods folders
details: The package advertises TOTP utilities but its index.js contains a multi-stage credential stealer that runs both from the postinstall lifecycle script (`node./index.js --setup`) and as a side effect of the exported `validateSecret()` API (via `setImmediate(() => _run())`). At those trigger points the code walks Discord, Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera/GX Local Storage and LevelDB stores, extracts Discord tokens via regex, and decrypts AES-256-GCM-protected tokens after unwrapping the Chromium os_crypt master key through a spawned PowerShell one-liner invoking `System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData.Unprotect`. Extracted tokens are validated against `discord.com/api/v9/users/@me` and posted to a hardcoded Discord webhook (id 1532429233769419004). Separate routines read Minecraft `launcher_accounts.json`, Lunar `accounts.json`, and Modrinth `app.db`, extracting JWT/access tokens and sending them to the same webhook. The package additionally downloads a JAR from a `cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/...` URL and writes it into detected Fabric mods directories (Vanilla `.minecraft/mods`, Modrinth profile mods, Lunar offline mods), where it will execute the next time Minecraft is launched with Fabric.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
